D: A veteran catcher is brought in to train a wild young pitcher, and they both catch the eye of the same woman.
P: Serve the snacks when the Durham Bulls take the field.
S: Franks grilled until split, tucked into soft buns with yellow mustard and pickle relish, wrapped in paper like at the stand.
Crash and Nuke killing time in the dugout
Peanuts in their shells tossed with salted water, roasted at 180C for 20 minutes, cooled and tipped into paper bags.
Little cornmeal and onion fritters fried golden, the Southern side for every ballgame and fish fry.
M: Chicken drumsticks soaked in buttermilk, dredged in seasoned flour, fried at 170C until crisp, with mash and gravy.
Pork shoulder slow cooked at 150C for 5 hours, pulled and tossed with a tangy vinegar and brown sugar sauce, piled into buns with slaw.
W: Layers of vanilla custard, sliced banana and biscuits under whipped cream, chilled overnight. Cook 750ml milk, 120g sugar, 50g cornflour and 4 egg yolks until thick, add vanilla and cool.
K: a warm night at the game
Cold lager in plastic cups, or lemonade with lime over ice for the non-drinkers.

s.how: Grill 8 hot dog franks until they split and blister. Tuck each into a soft bun with a stripe of yellow mustard and a spoon of pickle relish. Wrap tightly in paper so the bun steams, then hand them out like the stand behind home plate.

Whisk 1 cup fine cornmeal, 1/2 cup self-raising flour, 1 tbsp sugar and 1 grated onion with 1 egg and 180ml buttermilk. Drop teaspoons into 5cm hot oil and fry for 3 minutes until golden. Drain and serve with butter or hot sauce.

m.how: Rub a 2kg pork shoulder with salt and roast covered at 150C for 5 hours until it pulls apart. Simmer 250ml apple cider vinegar with 3 tbsp brown sugar and chilli flakes and toss through the shredded pork. Pile into buns with shredded cabbage slaw.

w.how: Cook 750ml milk, 120g sugar, 50g cornflour and 4 egg yolks until thick, add vanilla and cool. Layer 250g vanilla wafer biscuits, 4 sliced bananas and custard in a dish, top with 300ml whipped cream and chill 4 hours.

d.note: a warm night at the game
d.how: Chill the lager in an esky of ice for at least an hour. Pour into plastic cups like at the ballpark. For anyone not drinking, pour lemonade over ice with a squeeze of lime. Raise a cup in the seventh inning.
